title: sage-medical-integration-call-notes-2026-03-03
content:
Meeting: Sage Medical integration kickoff - 2026-03-03
Owner: Jordan Patel (SE)
Attendees: Sarah Kim (Sage - Product), Dr. Marco Alvarez (Sage - Clinical), Alex Chen (Redwood - Solutions), Priya Singh (Redwood - Security)

Purpose:
- Capture initial requirements and constraints for Sage Medical pilot (chat summaries + structured extraction of PHI-related events).
- Align on data residency, HIPAA controls, latency targets, and integration timeline.

Summary / Outcomes:
- Sage wants a pilot to power clinical note summarization + event extraction (meds, allergies, diagnoses). Output needs to be structured JSON that can be ingested by their EHR pipeline.
- Must be HIPAA-compliant; customer will require BAA and KMS-backed key management for any cloud-hosted data.
- Preferred deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) in us-east-1 initially; they may consider on-prem later.
- Latency requirement: 95th percentile < 1.5s per response for single-record summarization (typical length 500-1200 tokens). Throughput: ~30 qps during clinic hours (spiky).
- Accuracy: clinical fidelity is critical. They want sample-driven evals before rollout.

Requirements / Ask from Sage:
- Example data: 200 de-identified notes + 50 labeled examples for extraction mapping (they will provide week of 3/8).
- Schema: JSON schema for events (we sketched preliminary schema in Confluence link). Sage will confirm fields and priority.
- Auth: OAuth2 + client-cert for server-to-server calls. Secret rotation cadence must be documented.
- Auditing: Immutable audit log for inference requests (hashes ok), retention 1 year.

Technical notes / Gotchas:
- PHI handling: must ensure no long-term persistence of raw notes in hosted logs. Need to confirm if Redwood Private logs can be routed to Sage's SIEM. Action: Priya to confirm Redwood logging options and redact policy (due 3/6).
- Tokenization: many clinical abbreviations cause token bloat; need to test with Sage corpus to validate cost estimates.
- Model choice: propose using a fine-tuned open model (Redwood-Clinical-v1) quantized to reduce cost; fallback to non-quantized for high-sensitivity cases. Need to validate extraction recall/precision.
- Batching: typical client pattern is single-note per request; we can enable micro-batching but must preserve latency SLO. Consider prefix caching for repeated patient-context queries later.
- EHR integration: Sage uses HL7 FHIR for downstream ingestion. We should output JSON that maps cleanly into FHIR Observation/Condition resources. Action: Alex to draft mapping doc (due 3/10).

Security & Compliance:
- BAA required before any production data. Legal loop: CC Alyssa (legal) - Jordan to intro after this doc finalized.
- KMS/HSM: Sage requires customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key). Confirm Redwood Private supports CMEK in their VPC deployment. Action: infra contact (Ben) to confirm (due 3/5).
- Pen testing: Sage requests an external pentest window prior to go-live. Note this in timeline.

Performance / Cost notes:
- Rough cost estimate (placeholder): with quantized model on DGX-class nodes, expected ~ $0.004 / 1k tokens; needs refinement after tokenization tests.
- SLA ask: 99.9% uptime during clinic hours; Redwood Dedicated/Private SLA conversation needed for commercial terms.

Open questions:
1) Will Sage allow the initial pilot to use synthetic/pseudo-PHI for model tuning? They want to but need legal sign-off.
2) Exact FHIR resource mapping (which fields map to Observation vs Condition).
3) Do they need synchronous call pattern or are they ok with async processing with webhooks? (Sage prefers sync for clinician UX)

Next steps / Action items:
- Sage: provide 200 de-id notes + 50 labeled extraction examples (due 3/10) - Sarah (Sage)
- Jordan: intro to Alyssa (legal) and start BAA template (by 3/6)
- Priya: confirm logging/retention options and redact policy for Redwood Private (by 3/6)
- Ben (infra): confirm CMEK support in Private VPC and KMS integration steps (by 3/5)
- Alex: draft FHIR mapping + sample output JSON (by 3/10)
- Jordan/Alex: run tokenization/cost analysis on sample corpus once received (by 3/15)
- Schedule: 1:1 technical deep-dive (redwood infra + model team) week of 3/9. Jordan to propose slots.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Emphasize ability to do local KMS in Private deployment — big unlock for Sage.
- Prepare demo flow: example note -> Redwood API -> structured JSON -> ingest to FHIR. Keep demo with synthetic but realistic clinical terms.
- Consider optional feature: redaction step before sending to model (client-side or RW side?). Pros/cons: client-side keeps less risk but more dev work for Sage.

Related tickets / refs:
- JIRA-3421 (sage pilot scoping)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sage-integration-prototype#12 (early extractor)
- Confluence: SAGE-Integration-Overview (link above)

Priority: HIGH - pilot to start Q2.

-- Jordan
